item.title: ‘Threatened and discriminated’: Kumar Sangakkara alleges discrimination by Ryanair staff in Dublin
item.description: Former Sri Lanka captain Kumar Sangakkara has alleged that Ryanair staff threatened and discriminated against his family at an airport in Dublin, with his account triggering a discussion on social media. The Rajasthan Royals head coach took to X on Wednesday evening to share his experience, describing the encounter with the airline's gate personnel as shocking. He also called it his first unpleasant experience in Dublin, the capital of Ireland. “Has anyone experienced discriminatory gate personnel @Ryanair in Dublin? I, with my family, just did and it was shocking," Sangakkara tweeted on Wednesday evening. Sangakkara's post drew reactions from social media users, including fellow Sri Lankan Sanjiva Weerawarana, who spoke about his own experiences of discrimination while living and travelling overseas. “Kumar, I have experienced discrimination in every part of the West. I lived there for 16 years, travelled back and forth for another 25 and now I’m done," the individual replied. Responding to Weerawarana, Sangakkara acknowledged the distress such encounters can cause. “It’s quite jarring when you experience it," Sangakkara said. The exchange added to the discussion surrounding the former Sri Lankan skipper's allegations and the treatment of passengers by airline personnel. At the time of writing, Ryanair had not issued a response to Sangakkara's claims. Ryanair is an Irish ultra-low-cost airline headquartered in Swords, County Dublin. The incident has also brought attention to concerns about anti-Asian racism and xenophobia in Ireland, which can range from everyday prejudice and online abuse to physical assaults. Sangakkara's coaching career and international record Sangakkara, regarded as one of Sri Lanka's greatest cricketers, retired from international cricket in 2015 after a distinguished career across formats. As Rajasthan Royals coach, Sangakkara ended the franchise’s 17-year wait to reach another final during his first tenure. However, the Royals finished runners-up to Gujarat Titans. In 2026, Rajasthan bowed out in Qualifier 2, falling one win short of the final. Sangakkara's Test career began against South Africa in Galle on July 20, 2000, and concluded in Colombo after 134 matches. He accumulated 12,400 runs, including 38 centuries and 52 half-centuries. He finished one short of Australian great Donald Bradman's record of 12 double centuries. In ODIs, Sangakkara played 404 matches after making his debut in 2000, scoring 14,234 runs at an average of almost 42. His highest score was 169, while his tally included 25 centuries and 93 half-centuries. He brought his 50-over international career to an end after the 2015 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand. Sangakkara was part of Sri Lanka teams that finished runners-up at the 2007 and 2011 editions of the tournament.

item.title: Jorge Martin braced for “really difficult, painful” MotoGP weekend with broken arm
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin says he is pressing ahead with the Malaysian Grand Prix weekend despite expecting it to be “really difficult” and “really painful” to ride a MotoGP bike with a broken arm. The factory Aprilia rider followed an intensive recovery programme with his physiotherapist in the wake of his crash at the Australian Grand Prix, which left him with a fracture to the radius of his right arm. The Spaniard cleared his first hurdle on Thursday when he was declared fit by MotoGP’s doctor Angel Charte to take part in FP1. He will have to clear further medical tests on Friday before being allowed to race at the Sepang International Circuit. Arriving at the track on Thursday with a brace around his right wrist, Martin admitted that he was still feeling far from fully recovered, revealing he cannot even brush his teeth with his right hand. However, he insisted he had to at least attempt to ride this weekend to keep his title hopes alive against Ducati’s Marc Marquez . “I feel good, for sure. I could be worse, I could be better,” he said. “Let's see my condition, let's see my feeling, and then we will decide what to do next, if we continue with the GP or not. “The only thing I know is that my wrist is broken. I will try to ride with a broken wrist, so for sure it will be really difficult, it will be really painful. “I will try for sure because I'm in the title fight. Otherwise I will be in my house with a cast for one month. "Let's see how much a limitation it is for the riding style. For sure, it's the right hand, where the brake and the throttle are. It's a right-corner circuit. So overall it doesn't look great, but let's see tomorrow. “I still cannot brush my teeth. I do it with my left hand, so I cannot do almost anything, but maybe I can ride. “I'm not really optimistic, not too pessimistic, because after five days I'm here and I can ride. So it's already crazy. item.title: PSG eye Bayer Leverkusen star Ibrahim Maza ahead of January transfer window
item.description: PSG eye Bayer Leverkusen star Ibrahim Maza ahead of January transfer window Ibrahim Maza's impressive development at Bayer Leverkusen has attracted the attention of Paris Saint-Germain , with the French champions reportedly making contact with the player's representatives. Leverkusen want to reward the attacking midfielder with a new contract, but an agreement is not expected to be reached quickly. Maza joined Leverkusen from Hertha BSC for €12 million in 2025 and has established himself as a key player very quickly. After ten appearances this season, the 20-year-old has recorded three goals and three assists, already matching half of his total goal contributions from the previous campaign. His performances have also significantly increased his market value, which recently rose to €50 million , according to Transfermarkt. According to Sky Germany, Leverkusen are working on an early extension of Maza's contract, which currently runs until 2030. However, negotiations are expected to take time, while interest from several European clubs continues to grow. PSG are the newest among the clubs monitoring the Algerian international and have reportedly already contacted his representatives to express their interest. The French champions are considering a move as early as the January transfer window, with injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and recurring fitness problems for Ousmane Dembélé reportedly contributing to their desire to strengthen their attacking options. Manchester City were also said to have shown strong interest in Maza last summer, while Arsenal and Aston Villa have recently been linked with the attacking midfielder as well. Leverkusen see similarities with Florian Wirtz Maza's dribbling ability, vision and attacking output have drawn comparisons with former Leverkusen star Florian Wirtz, who joined Liverpool for €125 million last year. After Maza contributed a goal and an assist in Leverkusen's 2-1 victory over Freiburg, sporting director Simon Rolfes praised the youngster's qualities. "He's also a little dribbler; we've had that combination here before," Rolfes said, referring to the similarities with Wirtz. Head coach Carles Martínez also highlighted Maza's importance to the team, praising both his talent and his willingness to improve. "He's a very, very talented player; he gives us a lot. He's always ready and wants to improve," Martínez said. “With players like him, who are involved both offensively and defensively, we can keep getting better. The whole team played well, but the connection between Maza and Schick will be important.” Despite the growing attention and his rising market value, Maza has remained focused on his performances rather than individual recognition. "I always try to keep pushing, to keep training hard. And I hope that as a team, we can achieve our goals this year," he said. “The team's goals come first. If I can help with goals and assists, then I'm happy too. But of course, you also have your own ambitions.”

item.title: Confirmed: Real Madrid superstar nominated for La Liga Player of the Month award for October
item.description: Confirmed: Real Madrid superstar nominated for La Liga Player of the Month award for October Real Madrid have enjoyed a much-needed turnaround in La Liga this month, winning three consecutive matches and reducing Barcelona’s advantage at the top of the table to just three points. Kylian Mbappe has been central to that resurgence, delivering decisive performances when Jose Mourinho’s team needed him most. The French superstar has now been officially nominated for La Liga ‘s Player of the Month award for October. The nomination follows an impressive run that included a match-winning brace against Barça at the Spotify Camp Nou . Mbappe rewarded for impressive October performances Mbappe scored four goals in three league appearances during October, helping Real Madrid maintain a perfect record throughout the month. The 27-year-old’s month included two braces against Sevilla and Barça . Those performances took his goal tally to 11, placing him second behind Raphinha, who has scored 13. Mbappe faces competition from Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, Real Sociedad’s Goncalo Guedes, Atletico Madrid’s Alejandro Grimaldo and Elche goalkeeper Matias Dituro for the monthly award. The Frenchman was also nominated for the award back in September, but was pipped to it by eventual winner Raphinha. Mbappe continues to lead Mourinho’s attacking project Mbappe narrowly missed out on the 2026 Ballon d’Or to Harry Kane , but his season has started on a brilliant note regardless. His performances have also benefited from Jose Mourinho’s recent tactical adjustments. Arda Guler’s creativity, Yan Diomande’s movement and Eduardo Camavinga’s ability to carry the ball forward have created opportunities for the French striker. The team is finding ways to put Mbappe in goalscoring positions. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) If there is one thing Mbappe knows how to do better than most people in the world, it is to find the back of the net. The Clasico offered a convincing example of this, with Mbappe profiting from Los Blancos ‘ tactical set-up and remaining clinical in decisive moments. The biggest positive for Madrid is that they are finding ways to supply their talismanic scorer rather than asking him to do everything on his own. Whether Mbappe wins the monthly award remains to be seen, but there is no doubt that his October performances have brought Madrid right back into the La Liga title race.

item.title: Charles Barkley calls out Nikola Jokic over his ‘not real fans’ comments
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Charles Barkley has called out Nikola Jokic after the Denver Nuggets star criticised supporters who booed the team during their disappointing start to the NBA season. Jokic suggested that fans who booed the Nuggets did not need to attend their games anymore, sparking a backlash over his comments. The Serbian centre later doubled down on his stance , insisting that those supporters were not “real fans”. Charles Barkley explains why Nikola Jokic is wrong about Nuggets fans Speaking on SiriusXM NBA Radio, Barkley argued that players must accept criticism from supporters when results do not go their way. The NBA legend said: “Him calling out the fans was like, because you know fans are sensitive. They’re like, screw you, we pay you all that money. We’ve been following you, and we love you. And he says, like, yeah, don’t come to the game. Like, no, you can’t play bad.” Barkley believes that booing is part of the relationship between teams and their supporters, particularly when performances fall below expectations. He pointed to a recent Philadelphia 76ers game against the Cleveland Cavaliers as an example of how quickly fans can change their reactions when a team starts playing better. The Sixers were booed during the first half before receiving cheers after mounting a comeback. Barkley used the example to explain why Jokic should not take criticism personally. He added: “[Philadelphia 76ers fans] were booing like hell in the first half [against the Cleveland Cavaliers], and then the Sixers came back, and they were cheering. That’s how this thing works. We love you when things are going good. We’re gonna turn on you when things are going bad.” The former NBA star also compared the situation to how journalists treat athletes, arguing that praise and criticism naturally come with the territory. His comments come as Denver look to recover from a slow start, having opened the season with a 1-2 record before their NBA Cup action. The Nuggets are expected to compete among the Western Conference’s leading teams, with Jokic remaining central to their ambitions. However, Barkley’s criticism highlights the pressure that comes with those expectations, particularly when a team’s performances leave supporters frustrated. item.title: “This is a Farewell Tour For The King Fellas” – NBA World Reacts as LeBron James Gets Blocked on a Chase-Down and Has His Ankles Snatched
item.description: LeBron James got his showed blocked by Jalen Slawson © X/ @Pacers LeBron James nearly found himself on the receiving end of two highlight reels by the Indiana Pacers players on Wednesday. First, the 41-year-old got blocked on a chase-down by former second-round pick Jalen Slawson in the first quarter. Second, late in the fourth, James almost braced for another lowlight after Andrew Nembhard crossed him up and snapped his ankles. However, the Pacers guard missed the 3-point shot. Here’s the video of Slawson’s block on James: Here’s Nembhard’s move on James: James getting swatted on a chase-down or having his ankle snapped is almost unheard of in his 23 seasons. After falling prey to both incidents in the same game, the videos went viral and garnered thousands of reactions from NBA fans. “This is a farewell tour for the King fellas,” one fan said. LeBron James finds jump shot rhythm; finishes with a double-double as the 76ers rally to beat the Pacers Leaving the couple of lowlights aside, LeBron James actually had a decent outing in his fourth game for the 76ers. James struggled with his jump shooting in the first three games, going 1-for-10 from deep. According to the NBA’s tracking data , James shot less than 30.0% from five feet and beyond. However, things went the opposite way in Wednesday’s game, which the 76ers won 114-109 despite trailing by 13 to start the fourth. James took eight shots outside the paint and made four. That total included a couple of 3s. He was 2-for-3 from long range. James also converted a crucial 3 in the fourth quarter to cut the Pacers’ lead to five with 8:32 left. James shot 5-for-12 overall after making only one shot in the paint on four attempts. Nevertheless, he compensated for his inefficient scoring inside the paint by dishing 10 assists without turning the ball over. James scored 13 points, making it his second double-double in a Sixers uniform. item.title: 'Just call me Harry' - Kane downplays 'Sir' title talk as Bayern Munich star reacts to knighthood buzz following Ballon d'Or win
item.description: FC Bayern München v 1. FC Magdeburg - DFB Cup 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Harry Kane has addressed the growing speculation regarding a potential knighthood after becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or. The Bayern Munich striker admitted that while the honour would be life-changing, he remains grounded amidst the national frenzy. Kane addresses royal honour speculation The footballing world is currently buzzing with the possibility of the Bayern talisman being included in the upcoming New Year’s Honours List. Following his historic victory in London, where he became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or , a national debate has erupted regarding a potential trip to Buckingham Palace . Despite the prestige associated with such an accolade, the 33-year-old remains characteristically grounded about the prospect of becoming a knight of the realm. When questioned about the possibility of King Charles III conferring the honour upon him, Kane displayed his trademark humility while acknowledging the significance of the gesture. "I certainly wouldn't say no – I really appreciate it," Kane told Bild . "If it came to that, it would be incredible and something I'd be incredibly proud of. But I don't want to get too carried away with it right now." The striker was quick to point out that the formal title might take some getting used to in his everyday life. Regarding the "Sir Harry Kane" moniker, he laughed: "It sounds good, but it would feel kind of strange if everyone called me Sir – so for now, I'll just stick with Harry." Reflecting on a historic Ballon d'Or victory It has been a whirlwind week for the former Tottenham man, who returned to his home city to collect the Golden Ball. The ceremony was a departure from his usual comfort zone on the pitch, involving a tense wait before his name was finally called out as the winner. Kane admitted to feeling a different kind of pressure while sitting in the audience, wondering if he would truly be the one to follow in the footsteps of Sir Stanley Matthews. The support from the global football community has been significant, with the striker receiving a flood of messages across various platforms. "Yes, a truly crazy week. What an unbelievable evening on Monday! Of course, there was a lot of nervousness involved – it was a completely different set of emotions than at a football match," he revealed. "There was a lot of waiting involved, and I kept imagining what it would be like if I actually won. But honestly, it was just something really special. The support I received from friends, family, and fans – through messages, on social media – was almost overwhelming. So many congratulations! item.title: Vikings Get Concerning Update on Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors
item.description: (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings are reportedly one of several teams interested in Jonathan Taylor. The Indianapolis Colts have already begun moving key players, trading DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson on October 27, raising questions about whether Taylor could be next to leave Indianapolis. However, despite the Colts having a mini-fire sale this week, making two big trades in one day, Indianapolis might not be ready to pull the trigger on any trade involving their running back. NFL insider Jordan Schultz sounded bullish on a potential Taylor trade ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline when sharing what he knows about the situation. “I don’t think [the Colts are] done,” Schultz said in an Oct. 28 video from SiriusXM NFL Radio . “I don’t know if anything’s imminent in terms of another deal. They moved quickly yesterday with the two trades, and I had talked about the Colts being real sellers and how Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were at the top of that list. Milwaukee defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5, ending a wait that stretched back to the franchise’s arrival in Wisconsin. As the Brewers celebrated at Tropicana Field, Yelich was asked about Bob Uecker, the beloved broadcaster who spent more than five decades calling their games and died before seeing the team reach the top. Christian Yelich Delivers Emotional Bob Uecker Message After World Series During an on-field interview with FOX’s Ken Rosenthal, Yelich was asked what Uecker would have been thinking as Milwaukee celebrated its first championship. Milwaukee had reached the World Series only once before Wednesday, losing to the St. Louis Cardinals in seven games in 1982. But there they were, these pesky, potent, prolific Brewers, joyfully embracing after a five-game win in the best-of-seven series over the Tampa Bay Rays. item.title: It might be all over, key Liverpool player set to leave
item.description: It might be all over, key Liverpool player set to leave According to a recent report, it's all over for a key Liverpool player who could leave the club in weeks. Julian Ward has a massive job on his hands as Liverpool's sporting director, and his first priority should be pretty obvious. The Reds need to finally address the defensive midfield problem that has been hanging over Anfield for the best part of three years. Ever since Fabinho left the club in 2023, Liverpool have been searching for someone who can fill that void. And honestly, it's been a pretty painful process. The Reds have had plenty of opportunities to get it right, but things just haven't worked out. It started with Aurélien Tchouaméni, who ultimately chose Real Madrid instead of moving to Anfield. Then came the whole Romeo Lavia and Moisés Caicedo saga. Liverpool were prepared to spend big on both players, only for them to end up at Chelsea. The Reds eventually settled for Wataru Endo, who brought experience and commitment but was never really a long-term solution to the problem. Martin Zubimendi was another target who looked capable of transforming Liverpool's midfield. Unfortunately, he decided to remain in San Sebastián before eventually joining Mikel Arteta at Arsenal. How Liverpool have 'fixed' the holding midfield situation In the meantime, Liverpool have had to find ways to cope with the situation. Ryan Gravenberch has done an admirable job filling the No.6 role, while Alexis Mac Allister has also been deployed there when needed. Both players bring plenty of quality, but neither quite offers the defensive security Liverpool have been missing. The Reds need someone who can protect the back four, win duels, read danger and allow the more attack-minded midfielders to play with greater freedom. There is, however, an encouraging development in Trey Nyoni. The youngster's ability to read the game and operate as a deep-lying playmaker gives Liverpool another intriguing option from within their own academy. But potential alone won't solve everything. Ward needs to find the right balance between developing young talent and bringing in proven quality. Liverpool have waited long enough for a proper Fabinho replacement. It's time to get it right. Alexis Mac Allister to be sacrificed by Liverpool But it appears that Liverpool are currently operating under the guise of one in, one out in the midfield department. This means that Mac Allister, who has been imperative to the club's success this season could leave the Reds in order to pave the way for a more defensive minded midfielder to come in. item.description: Five Things Learned: Manchester City 2-2 (4-3 pens) Brighton & Hove Albion (Carabao Cup Fourth Round) Man City's penalty shoot-out hero: Geronimo Rulli! Manchester City took down Fabian Hurzeler's high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion on penalties to advance into the quarter-final stage of the 2026/27 Carabao Cup. Enzo Maresca's side arrived at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday looking to carry on the defence of silverware they won in March, having comfortably dispatched of Norwich City last time out in the competition, and finding things much harder against Brighton. The Seagulls took the lead on the half-hour mark as Georginio Rutter found Malick Yalcouye to blast past Geronimo Rulli from close range despite suggestions of offside. Amid continued Brighton & Hove Albion pressure, City got themselves level with a superb curving long-distance strike from Mateo Kovacic. After going in level at the half-time interval, Enzo Maresca's men soon found themselves behind again as Georginio Rutter slotted the ball into the corner within 90 seconds of the restart. Manchester City survived the storm and, thanks to some inspired play from Jeremy Doku, found themselves putting pressure back on the visitors. This saw the Citizens win a free-kick on the edge of the box, dispatched fortunately by Rayan Cherki via Vitor Reis' heel. Despite chances at both ends, the two sides could not be separated in the remainder of the 90 minutes and the match went straight to a penalty shootout following the full-time whistle. Phil Foden, Enzo Fernandez, and Jeremy Doku all scored, but Mateo Kovacic saw his attempt saved by Brighton's Jason Steele. Thankfully, Geronimo Rulli saved Yasin Ayari's effort, and Rayan Cherki hammered in his spot-kick, leaving the Argentine keeper to save Lewis Dunk's shot to win the tie. In a week when Manchester City's first-choice goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma has faced mounting criticism, Geronimo Rulli picked the perfect moment to announce himself to the sky blue faithful. After a rather uneventful debut against Norwich City in the previous round of the Carabao Cup, the Argentine international was back in the starting line-up for the visit of Brighton & Hove Albion. His fellow goalkeeper Donnarumma conceded from both shots on target against Aston Villa over the weekend, but Rulli put in a better showing on Wednesday night. As the Brighton pressure mounted, he gave a decent account of himself in the 90 minutes before turning into the hero during the penalty shootout. Producing saves to stop both Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk, the Argentine won both the match and the hearts of Manchester City fans in just his second game for the club. 2. item.title: ‘Our leader’ – Charles Barkley tears up while giving emotional Ernie Johnson tribute
item.description: Photo by Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Turner Sports Inside the NBA is set to lose a legend after Ernie Johnson announced his retirement at the end of the season. Charles Barkley got very emotional when addressing it on set. Ernie Johnson is arguably the most legendary broadcaster in the world of basketball. The iconic host of Inside the NBA began the show in 1990, and has helped it grow into one of the most popular and beloved programmes in sports television history. NBA legend Charles Barkley has been working with Johnson for 26 years, since he joined TNT as a studio analyst in 2000. The duo, along with Kenny ‘The Jet’ Smith and Shaquille O’Neal, have been instrumental to the show’s success. So naturally, when Ernie announced his retirement the other day, Barkley’s tribute to him was as heartfelt as it was emotional. Charles Barkley opens up on ‘honour and privilege’ of amazing journey with Ernie Johnson What made Inside the NBA so unique and special is the way O’Neal, Barkley, and Smith’s personalities all play off one another. Johnson has manfully handled the task of ensuring that they stay on track, while never letting their candid hilarity get lost in the process. He has been a mentor to all three, and his bond with Barkley goes well beyond the show. The duo has worked together on many other projects, and they are close friends on top of that. Barkley’s tribute to Johnson encompassed all of that and more. “That was tough,” Barkley said about the retirement announcement while tearing up. “We knew the day was coming, but still tough. Been here for 26, 27 years and it’s been an honour and a privilege to work with you all this time. And Kenny and Shaq and all the amazing people behind the scenes. “It’s been an amazing journey. You’ve been our leader. Unquestionable leader. The question I’m asked the most… ‘Is Ernie Johnson as good a person as he seems?’ And I say, ‘Man, he’s better than that.’ I just want to say thank you. Thank you for being our leader for all these years. Even though I knew it was coming, it’s still hard, brother… All I can say Ernie, is thank you.” While Barkley is possibly the closest person to Johnson professionally, his feelings are shared by a lot of the basketball world. Very few figures are as universally beloved in a space as Ernie is in basketball, so his departure from the screen will be a sad moment for the entire community.
